name: Hot-aisle containment
pitch: Stop hot and cold air from mixing. Cheap, boring, effective.
whyItMatters: Some green moves simply pay: less fan and chiller energy for the same compute.
source: EU Code of Conduct on Data Centre Energy Efficiency, best practices (airflow management)

name: Run the room warmer
pitch: Raise server inlet air to 27 °C. Free, but hardware works a bit harder.
whyItMatters: ASHRAE's recommended inlet range goes up to 27 °C: less cooling, slightly more stress on the hardware.
source: ASHRAE TC 9.9 Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments (recommended range 18-27 °C)

name: Free cooling
pitch: Use outside air instead of chillers whenever it is cold enough.

nordic-fjord.note: You already run cool here: real gain, but smaller.

sun-belt.note: Outside air is 40 °C half the year. Free cooling barely works here.

whyItMatters: Where you build decides how much energy cooling needs. The same upgrade is great in the north and nearly useless in the desert.
source: Free cooling potential depends on climate (EU Code of Conduct on Data Centre Energy Efficiency)

name: Evaporative cooling
pitch: Cool with evaporating water. Cheap and very energy-efficient.

sun-belt.note: Works wonders in dry heat. You are now competing with farms and towns for water.

nordic-fjord.note: Plenty of water here, but little to gain: it is already cold.

whyItMatters: Saving energy by consuming water is a transfer of impact, not a free win. Where water is scarce, it is a time bomb.
source: Water-energy trade-off in datacenter cooling (WUE metric, The Green Grid)

name: Direct liquid cooling
pitch: Pipe coolant straight to the chips in a closed loop.
whyItMatters: Removing heat where it is made cuts both energy and water, but retrofits are expensive and add a new failure mode.
source: Industry literature on direct-to-chip liquid cooling (order of magnitude)

name: Heat reuse network
pitch: Pipe this hall's waste heat to warm nearby homes.

nordic-fjord.note: Long winters: everyone wants your heat.

whyItMatters: Almost every kWh a server uses ends up as heat. Selling it to a district heating network turns waste into warm homes.
source: EU Energy Efficiency Directive (EU) 2023/1791 (waste heat recovery for datacenters above 1 MW)

name: Measure everything
pitch: Real-time metering of energy, carbon and water per room and per client.
whyItMatters: You can't reduce what you don't measure, and you can't prove a green claim without data.
source: AFNOR Spec 2314, General framework for frugal AI (CGDD/SRI/Ecolab): measurement tools and indicators

name: Keep servers 6 years
pitch: Repair and reuse instead of replacing every 4 years.
whyItMatters: Manufacturing is a big share of hardware's footprint. Using servers longer avoids a whole replacement cycle, at the price of more breakdowns.
source: ADEME-Arcep 2022 study on the environmental footprint of digital in France (manufacturing dominates equipment impacts)

name: Certified refurb and recycling
pitch: Resell, refurbish, and properly recycle every retired server.
whyItMatters: Only about a fifth of the world's e-waste is documented as properly collected and recycled.
source: Global E-waste Monitor 2024 (UNITAR/ITU): 22.3 % formally collected and recycled in 2022

name: Always the newest chips
pitch: Replace servers every 2 years to stay on the cutting edge.
whyItMatters: New chips do more per watt, but each early replacement scraps tonnes of hardware whose manufacturing emissions are already spent.
source: Game design, grounded in life-cycle assessment logic (embodied vs. operational emissions)

name: Overclock and cram
pitch: Pack more servers in this hall and push them harder.
whyItMatters: Running hot and dense squeezes more money out of every rack, until hardware starts dying young.
source: Game design

name: GenAI GPU cluster
pitch: Fill this hall with GPUs and ride the AI boom. Power-hungry.
whyItMatters: AI demand is real, but chasing every hype project locks in power-hungry hardware for uses nobody questioned.
source: IEA, Energy and AI (2025): datacenter electricity demand projected to roughly double by 2030

name: "Carbon neutral" badge
pitch: Buy cheap offsets, put a green leaf on the website, charge a premium.
whyItMatters: Offsets don't remove your emissions. EU rules now ban 'carbon neutral' product claims based on offsetting.
source: Directive (EU) 2024/825 on empowering consumers for the green transition (bans neutrality claims based on offsetting)

name: Frugal AI checklist
pitch: Before hosting any AI workload: is AI needed? Is there a lighter option?
whyItMatters: Step one of the AFNOR frugal-AI method: question the need. Some business walks away; what stays is worth hosting.
source: AFNOR Spec 2314, General framework for frugal AI: 'Question the need' and 'Identify all possible solutions'

name: Model right-sizing service
pitch: Help clients compress, distill and shrink their models.
whyItMatters: Smaller, compressed models often do the job with a fraction of the compute. Watch out: cheaper compute invites more use.
source: AFNOR Spec 2314: favour frugal models, use compression, A/B test performance vs. resources

name: Frugal-IT training
pitch: Train your team and your clients on responsible digital practices.
whyItMatters: AFNOR ranks awareness and skills first: the best gain-to-effort ratio of all best practices.
source: AFNOR Spec 2314: 'Managing skills and increasing awareness on frugal AI' (highest gain/effort theme)

name: Sufficiency pledge
pitch: Publicly cap your growth. Big enough is big enough.
whyItMatters: Efficiency without limits often means more total consumption (rebound effect). Sufficiency means deciding how much is enough.
source: AFNOR Spec 2314 (rebound effect, planetary boundaries)

name: Closed-loop water
pitch: Recycle cooling water instead of drawing fresh water.
whyItMatters: Recycling water cuts withdrawals, but pumps and chillers use more energy: a real trade-off between water and carbon.
source: Water-energy trade-off in cooling design (WUE vs. PUE, The Green Grid)

name: Smoke scrubbers
pitch: Filter soot and sulfur out of the chimney. Not the CO2.
whyItMatters: Scrubbers clean the air locally, but the climate damage of coal stays the same.
source: Game design

name: Cheap lignite
pitch: Burn low-grade brown coal. 30 % cheaper fuel.
whyItMatters: Lignite is the dirtiest coal: cheaper fuel, more CO2 and more pollution per MWh.
source: Game design

name: Carbon capture
pitch: Capture most of the CO2. Costs a lot and eats a fifth of the output.
whyItMatters: Capture works on paper; in practice it is expensive and uses part of the plant's own power.
source: IPCC AR5 WGIII (2014): CCS energy penalty and costs (order of magnitude)

name: Heat recovery
pitch: Reuse exhaust heat to make more power from the same gas.
whyItMatters: Efficiency gains at the plant mean less fuel for the same MWh.
source: Game design

name: Methane leak checks
pitch: Find and fix gas leaks on the supply line.
whyItMatters: Leaked methane warms the planet far more than CO2 over 20 years; measuring leaks is cheap.
source: IEA Global Methane Tracker (order of magnitude)

name: Certified local wood
pitch: Only wood from sustainably managed local forests. Pricier.
whyItMatters: Biomass is only low-carbon if the forest regrows; certification and short supply chains help.
source: Game design

name: Imported pellets
pitch: Cheap wood pellets shipped from overseas forests.
whyItMatters: Shipping pellets across oceans from cleared forests can make biomass worse than gas.
source: Game design

name: Bigger rotors
pitch: Longer blades catch more wind: +30 % output.
whyItMatters: Repowering an existing site gets more clean MWh from the same land.
source: Game design

name: Battery storage
pitch: Store sunny or windy hours for the calm ones.
whyItMatters: Batteries smooth renewables so your halls stay on; they also need mined metals.
source: Game design

name: Sun trackers
pitch: Panels that follow the sun: +25 % output.
whyItMatters: More output from the same land, at the price of moving parts.
source: Game design

name: Fish ladders
pitch: Let fish swim past the dam and keep a minimum river flow.
whyItMatters: A little less power, a living river downstream.
source: Game design
